name: Neumorphism
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a directly named source-collection style. Uses raised or inset surfaces close to the shared background, paired soft highlights and directional shadows, restrained color, and clear state differences. Suitability beyond these stated cues is inferred.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to simple control panels when pressed and released states carry the story. Suggested hybrids suit settings, smart-home, or audio-app walkthroughs and supplied-data dashboards. Broader video or interactive HTML suitability is inferred; use HTML/CSS for real interface elements.
limitations: Soft depth can make state changes and edges hard to distinguish. Keep text, controls, and labels readable; do not rely on shadow depth alone. Recheck contrast on composited surfaces. Avoid invented interfaces, values, or audio assets. Supplemental provenance means this is a design reference, not a claimed canonical source style.
palette: Suggested tokens for new artwork only: background #E7EBED, foreground #303D49, accent #506F86 (three colors; no gradient). Task, brand, approved, semantic, and asset colors take precedence unchanged. Use accent for active/focus states or decoration; it fails the stated 4.5 normal-text target on background (4.421), so place body text on the main background. Validate actual surfaces; opaque two-color ratios do not guarantee readability over shadows or transparency.
motionAndInteraction: Animate apparent depth and shadow on press/release with consistent light direction and explicit state colors. Optional compatible choreography: causal control transitions, labeled data readouts in inset wells, scroll-driven cards or chapters, pointer tilt, swipe carousel, or story progression only when scene content supports it. HTML may use scroll, pointer, touch, keyboard, and focus; honor reduced motion. Video must derive state from seekable composition time, with reading holds and deterministic reverse/direct seeks, not live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory audio layer. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and explicit requirements. Actual playback, waveform, and spatial panning are separate choices; tilt does not imply audio or spatial sound. Keep speech intelligible, synchronize through the composition timeline, and check balance and clipping.
assetRequirements: Use supplied copy, assets, exact colors, and verified data without recoloring or invention. Load local fonts and assets; provide actual audio before depicting playback or waveforms. Dashboard values need units and labels. Interactive galleries need accurate image dimensions, responsive sources, alternatives, and fallback links; flattened artwork will not retain editable layers.
combinations: Use alone for simple press/release panels. Suggested hybrids: style-095 state-change choreography clarifies cause and result; style-097 readouts place verified values in inset wells, with flat data marks and no invented values or extra hues. Other motion patterns are optional and must fit scene geometry and narrative; reject unsupported depth, obscured copy, or conflicting progress drivers.
productionApproach: Style renderer owns surfaces, typography, shadows, and state colors; motion engine owns trajectories and easing, with one owner per property. HTML/CSS is the recommended renderer; GSAP is the primary seekable timeline, while Motion is optional only with explicit seek synchronization. HyperFrames owns video assembly, timing, media/audio sync, checks, and export; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation requires it, with reason recorded. Select tools for style fidelity first; optional Canvas/WebGL assets need deterministic time and explicit repaint. Validate contrast and opening, action, transition, closing, and full playback.
